title: Type-along · Returns with done-masks and a linear critic
prompt:
**Type the code yourself, line by line.** The ghost text shows what to write next and the note above the editor explains the line you are on. Provided blocks fill in automatically when you press Enter.

Actor-critic code is mostly careful array work on a **rollout**: a fixed number of steps that may span several episodes. On a hand-made trajectory and a tiny corridor you will practise:

- lining up V(sₜ₊₁) with step t via `np.append(values[1:], last_value)`
- a **backward discounted sum** with **done-masking** `(1 − doneₜ)` and a bootstrap value at the end
- a **linear critic** fitted by gradient descent: `err = prediction − target`, `w -= lr * X.T @ err / N`
- the `(N, 1)` vs `(N,)` broadcasting trap and `reshape(-1, 1)`

Press **F1** on any word (e.g. `np.append`) to open its reference in the **DOCS** tab. When you are done: **Run**, then **Check**. The next exercises — GAE and A2C on CartPole — use the same tools with no ghost text.
